quiz.q: You close a file's tab in the canvas. What happens to the project?
options: The project is deleted from the workspace
Nothing — the project stays open in Package Explorer
quiz.explain: Closing a tab is not closing the project; use right-click → Close Project for that.

quiz.q: You deleted project `dummy` without ticking "Delete project contents on disk". Creating a new project named `dummy` now fails. Why?
options: The project is still in Exchange
The project folder still exists in the workspace on disk
Studio forbids reusing project names forever
quiz.explain: Without the checkbox the project is only removed from Studio; delete the leftover folder from the workspace (or delete with the checkbox).

quiz.q: Nine projects are open and you want only the current one. Which option is quickest?
quiz.explain: Close Unrelated Projects closes all other projects (without deleting them).

quiz.q: How do you share a project with a colleague without a code repository?
options: Export it as a Mule Deployable Archive (JAR) and they import it via File → Import → Anypoint Studio → Packaged mule application (.jar)
Publish the canvas to Runtime Manager
quiz.explain: Export creates a JAR; share it via a common location, and the colleague imports the JAR.

quiz.q: On the Export dialog, what is the effect of exporting a lightweight package without modules and dependencies?
options: It can be imported into Studio but won't be deployable to CloudHub
It is deployable to CloudHub but not importable
quiz.explain: The dialog note says a lightweight package without modules and dependencies won't deploy to CloudHub but can be imported into Studio.

quiz.q: Importing a JAR shows "A project with name ... already exists" and Finish stays disabled. What do you do?
options: Change the project name in the import dialog
quiz.explain: The import name must not clash with an existing project in the workspace; the demo imported it under a new name.

quiz.q: Two files are modified and you press Ctrl+S. What happens?
options: Only the active file is saved; the other still shows a `*`
Neither is saved until you Build
quiz.explain: Ctrl+S saves the active file; Save All (Ctrl+Shift+S) saves all modified files.

quiz.q: Build Automatically is disabled. What must you do after changing a flow?
options: Stop and redeploy the application yourself
quiz.explain: With Build Automatically on (the default), saving rebuilds and redeploys; with it off, you redeploy manually.

quiz.q: After running a project many times with changes you see odd behavior from stale build output. Which Project menu option helps?
quiz.explain: Clean deletes generated build output (JARs in `target/`); then deploy again.

quiz.q: You want to run locally against the UAT database's property file. Which option lets you specify such settings?
options: Run As → Mule Application with defaults
quiz.explain: Run/Debug Configurations run with specific settings, such as which environment's property file to load.

quiz.q: You accidentally closed the Mule Debugger tab. How do you get it back?
options: Window → Show View → Other… → Mule Debugger
quiz.explain: Show View reopens closed tabs; Window → Perspective → Reset Perspective also restores the default layout.

quiz.q: What is a workspace in Anypoint Studio?
options: The folder where Studio creates and stores projects
quiz.explain: Studio shows only the current workspace's projects; switch with File → Switch Workspace, e.g. if a workspace gets corrupted.

cards.back: Package Explorer (left) · Canvas (centre) · Mule Palette (right) · bottom tabs: properties, Console, Problems, Search, Mule Debugger, MUnit Coverage/Errors.
Lists all projects created or imported in the current workspace, sorted alphabetically.
Central working area with Message Flow, Global Elements and Configuration XML tabs.

cards.front: Connector not in the Mule Palette?
cards.back: Add Modules → search Exchange → build a custom connector only if none exists.
Shows logs printed during deployment and request processing (Run or Debug).
**Next processor** (one step), **Resume** (to next breakpoint or end), **x+y** evaluate expression.
After writing MUnit tests: how many components and what percentage of each file are covered.
Close: project stays in Studio and workspace. Delete: removed from Studio; removed from disk only with "Delete project contents on disk".
Closes all projects except the selected one (does not delete them).
Right-click → Export → Mule → Anypoint Studio Project to Mule Deployable Archive → produces a JAR.
File → Import → Anypoint Studio → Packaged mule application (.jar) → choose JAR and a non-clashing project name.
Machine-readable, deployable archive of the project (the XML code is human-readable).
Ctrl+S saves the active file; Ctrl+Shift+S saves all. A `*` on a tab means unsaved.
Enabled by default: saving rebuilds and redeploys. If disabled, redeploy manually.
Deletes generated build output (JARs in `target/`) to clear stale artifacts.
Run with specific settings — e.g. which environment's property file to use.
Window → Show View reopens closed tabs (Console, Mule Palette, Other… → Mule Debugger).
Window → Perspective → Reset Perspective restores the default panel layout.

cards.front: Mule Design vs. Mule Debug mode
cards.back: Design for regular development; Debug rearranges panels for stepping through flows. Toggle at top-right.
Searches across projects; results in the Search tab with file and line number.
Shows the Studio version (e.g. 7.12.0). Mule 4.x refers to the runtime, not Studio.
The folder where Studio stores projects. A fresh one contains only `.metadata`.
To keep separate project sets, or to recover when a project/workspace is corrupted. File → Switch Workspace → Other…
